- When sentiment turns negative sharply (especially after a spike), model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment remains high for 3+ consecutive days, model often overestimates — apply downward bias of 3–7% to avoid “sentiment inflation”.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment, model frequently overshoots — cap forecast at 1.5x recent high if sentiment >0.8 for 2+ days.
- If news volume drops below 2.0 for 2+ days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast by 2–5% to reflect reduced market noise.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low and trending downward — add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment <0.3 and declining.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often misses the drop — adjust forecast down 3–8% for 2–3 days after such events.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3 days, forecast should be adjusted up by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the cycle — reduce forecast by 3–6% if sentiment is high and price is above 80.00.
